lots.guide_summary: 1 sold (close, not same item), 0 unsold, 0 asking. Only guide is a Napoleon III boulle serpentine jardiniere at GBP 200 hammer (about AUD 378) in Dec 2025. Rate GBP 1 = AUD 1.889.
lots.working: No same-item SOLD entry survives, so keep_max_hammer = 0 and flip_max_hammer = 0 under the rules. For reference only (not a max bid): if the Lots Road boulle piece were accepted as a same-item comp, keep = 378/1.22 = 309.8 -> 305; flip = (378 less 15% selling fee = 321) / 2.44 = 131.6 -> 130. All-in cost = hammer x 1.22, pickup only. Researcher had no entries; I added one close SOLD found through the Auctionet API. Checked and dropped: Lawrences Napoleon III parquetry jardiniere and cover GBP 220 (Jan 2024) because it is an 84cm standing jardiniere on legs, a different form; Balclis Louis XV style Napoleon III rosewood marquetry planter (unsold, top bid EUR 45, est EUR 140, Mar 2023, and unsold no bids est EUR 100, Nov 2023) because it is an 80cm standing planter, a different form.
lots.confidence_reason: No mark, no size given, period versus later reproduction unresolved, and only one close (not same-item) sold comp.
lots.condition: Vertical crack/split in the veneer on the handle end (clear in photo 6) and a split at a panel join on the front (photo 2); gallery rim slightly uneven; interior black lining worn and dusty; base studs and mounts appear complete in the photos; gilding looks bright, which may mean regilding or later manufacture.
lots.key_photo_findings: Six photos. Burr veneer with strong red figuring, ebonised studded plinth, dolphin feet at the corners, lion-mask cartouche to each long side, rococo scroll handles at the ends, pierced foliate gallery. Crack in the veneer running down from under the handle to the base (photo 6). No maker mark or stamp visible. No liner shown (interior lined in black fabric/paper rather than zinc).
lots.question_for_armitage: What are the dimensions? Is there a zinc or tin liner, or any stamp underneath? How long and how open is the crack in the veneer on the handle end, and is the veneer lifting? Does it appear 19th century or a later reproduction (are the mounts cast bronze or spelter)?
lots.dropped_entries: Researcher carried no entries. Dropped from my own search: Lawrences parquetry jardiniere and cover GBP 220 (standing form on legs, 84cm); Balclis rosewood marquetry planter twice unsold (standing form, 80cm).
lots.score_reason: Credible Napoleon III style decorative piece; the closest sale is about AUD 378 hammer, but the crack, unknown size and possible later manufacture pull the likely value down into the AUD 100-250 band.

lots.what_it_is: Blue cloth album titled 'Spurlings Tasmanian Post Cards' holding about 36 Spurling real photo postcards (A-series, e.g. A503, A562, A632, A741, A626), views of Launceston and Cataract Gorge, St Helens, Port Arthur, Queenstown and Mt Lyell, about 1920s-1940s.
lots.working: No SOLD evidence, so keep_max_hammer = 0 and flip_max_hammer = 0.
lots.confidence_reason: Identification is clear from the photos, but there is no price evidence of any kind.
lots.condition: Album cover and spine worn and rubbed. Card fronts look clean and sharp with good contrast; cards appear mounted on grey album pages with numbers written in pencil beside them. Whether cards are glued or in corners, and the backs, cannot be seen.
lots.key_photo_findings: Nine photos: cover plus eight pages of four cards (about 36 cards, including photo 9). Spurling series captions legible on several, e.g. Launceston from Windmill Hill, Cataract Gorge, Brisbane St Launceston with tram and cars, Town Hall, Royal Park, illuminated fountain, St Helens hotels, Model Prison and Penitentiary Port Arthur, Queenstown and Mt Lyell, Iron Blow/Lake Margaret. Street scenes with period cars and trams are the more saleable cards.
lots.question_for_armitage: Are the cards glued to the pages or held in corners (can they be removed without damage)? Are the backs unused or postally used? Are there any cards beyond the eight pages shown?
lots.dropped_entries: None carried by the researcher. Earlier dropped items (Examiner three-album report, stampauctionnetwork estimates) stay dropped. Searches tried this pass: Auctionet API 'spurling' and 'tasmania postcards' (only Jack Spurling marine prints, unrelated). WebSearch budget exhausted (200 of 200). Lawsons search returned 404; Leonard Joel search returned only a script shell. eBay not tried (closed to us).
lots.score_reason: A themed album of about 36 Spurling real photo cards including street scenes is likely worth roughly AUD 100-250 on general knowledge, but that is unverified, so scored cautiously.
